title: 5 Reasons why to get a title search when buying property
description: A title search reveals vital details before buying. Learn five reasons why it’s a must for every property purchase.
imageAlt: Magnifying glass over house, symbolising title search in property buying
tags: baxter and mason property buyers agent sunshine coast
body:
Without a title search you could end up buying a property that you may never legally own or it may be in a zone that could cause changes to the area around you in years to come (this could be a good or a bad thing depending on the zoning and location) or the purchase may have restrictions which could possibly mean that it is deemed unusable for your intended use.

Baxter & Mason Property Buyers Agent Sunshine Coast aren’t lawyers but we do understand the importance of a title search when you purchase a property. AND when using our services, we will connect you with one of our trusted conveyancers that will do all of the relevant searches to ensure your property purchase is air tight.

But for now, let’s help you understand the importance of a property title search when buying a house, unit or land.

1. Ownership: A title search will reveal the current and previous owners of the property, including any changes in ownership, such as sales or transfers.

2. Encumbrances: The search will show any encumbrances or legal interests that affect the property, such as mortgages, liens, restrictive covenants, or easements.

3. Zoning: The title search will also show the zoning of the property, which is the classification attributed to the land by the local council. The zoning determines what types of buildings can be constructed on the property and how the land can be used.

4. Restrictions: The search can reveal any restrictions or prohibitions on the use of the land, such as environmental regulations, heritage designations, or government-placed restrictions.

5. Caveats: Lastly, a title search can reveal any caveats placed on the property, which are legal restrictions that someone has put in place to protect their interest in the land. It is important to know if there are any caveats on the property before purchasing or dealing with it.

title: Are duplex, triplex and dual key properties a good investment?
description: Considering duplex or dual key properties? Explore the pros, cons, and investment potential of these unique housing options.
imageAlt: Modern duplex building, symbolising multi-dwelling property investment
tags: baxter and mason property buyers agent
baxter and mason property buyers agent sunshine coast
body:
If you live in an older suburb like I do on the Sunshine Coast, you probably have seen many new “multi dwelling” properties popping up. Lots of knockdowns are being replaced with a duplex, triplex or a dual-key. All of these types of property in Queensland and across Australia are considered good investments due to the yield and or profits from sale of part of the property, but like any property purchase, it of course is dependent on the location and condition of the property.

Multi dwelling properties provide an opportunity for multiple streams of income, as well as potential for capital growth over time. It is important to do thorough research before investing in any type of property and also consider which configuration will work for your needs, budget and long-term investment.

Unsure of the difference between a duplex, triplex of a dual-key property? Below is a quick breakdown.

Duplex: This kind of property consists of two separate dwellings that are connected by a common fire wall. The two dwellings can either be attached or detached but are on two titles and can be sold off as two separate homes. Typically, one dwelling is used as a residence and the other is rented out as an investment. The land size on which these can be build can vary from different councils and zoning. Some zones these may be possible if it is submitted to council as code assessable.

Triplex: A triplex is a property that consists of three separate dwellings that are connected by a common fire wall. Like a duplex, the three dwellings can either be attached or detached but are on three titles and can be sold off as three separate homes. Typically, one dwelling is used as a residence and the other two are rented out as investments. Like a duplex, the land size on which a triplex can be build can vary from different councils and zoning.

Dual-key: A dual-key property is more commonly known as a house with a granny flat. Modern day versions of dual-keys resemble a type of duplex with a separate dwelling, attached or detached but currently most councils keep these properties on one title, which means that the two dwellings can’t be sold off as two properties but need to be sold all together. This type of property can provide a great investment opportunity because it can be used as separate residential units for rental income or as one large combined property for a single family i.e. a separate unit for grandparents or extended family. Like a duplex or a triplex, the land size, council and zoning will depict if you are allowed to build or create a dual-key property.

title: Are you on the road to financial freedom?
description: See how property investment can set you on the path to financial freedom — with strategies to grow wealth and secure your future.
imageAlt: Long road with financial freedom painted, symbolising property wealth journey

Investing in property can potentially put you on the road to financial freedom due to several factors:

1. Potential for capital growth
Historically, property prices in Australia have shown steady growth over the long term. By investing in the right location and property type, you can benefit from capital appreciation, allowing you to build wealth and increase your net worth over time.

2. Rental income
Owning an investment property allows you to generate rental income. By choosing a property in a high-demand area with strong rental yields, you can create a passive income stream that can cover mortgage repayments, property expenses, and potentially even provide extra cash flow for savings or other investments.

3. Tax advantages
Australia's tax system offers various incentives for property investors. For example, you can claim tax deductions on expenses related to owning and maintaining the property, including interest payments on your mortgage, property management fees, repairs, and insurance. These deductions can help reduce your overall taxable income and increase your cash flow.

4. Leverage and equity growth
Property investment allows you to leverage your capital by taking on a mortgage. By using borrowed funds to purchase a property, you can multiply your investment, potentially benefiting from both the property's appreciation and the rental income generated. As you pay down your mortgage, your equity in the property grows, providing you with the opportunity to leverage that equity for future investments or to purchase additional properties.

5. Diversification
Property investment provides diversification in your investment portfolio. By investing in real estate, you are adding an asset class that typically performs differently from stocks, bonds, or other financial investments. This diversification can help spread risk and provide stability to your overall investment strategy.

6. Long-term stability
Property investment is generally considered a long-term strategy. Over time, as you hold onto the property, you can benefit from market cycles and trends. Real estate has historically been a stable investment, with values tending to recover and even increase after economic downturns.

7. Retirement planning
Investing in property can be an effective way to plan for retirement. By building a portfolio of investment properties, you can generate ongoing rental income that will provide you with a regular cash flow during your retirement years. Additionally, owning properties can give you the option to downsize or sell them and use the proceeds to fund your retirement lifestyle.

It's important to note that investing in property involves risks, and it's crucial to do thorough research, consider market conditions, and seek professional advice before making any investment decisions.

It is the start of a new tax year, and it is never too early to think about how you can reduce your tax.

1. Tax Concessions: Tax breaks from the Government such as deductions for the cost of borrowing, depreciation expenses, repairs and maintenance, and land tax can help reduce the cost of owning an investment property.

2. Capital Gains Tax Exemption on sale: If an investor holds an investment property for at least 12 months and makes a profit from the sale, they may be eligible to have some of these profits exempted from capital gains tax.

3. Negative Gearing: If a property investor is paying more in interest or property related costs than the rent received, they may be able to claim some deductions on their tax return.

4. Land Tax Savings: Investors can often receive a discount on their land tax if the property is used for investment purposes (as opposed to owner occupation).

5. Positive Cash Flow: Though it is not a tax break, positive cash flow from rental income can help pay the mortgage on an investment property and provide extra financial breathing space.

title: Do you know the local council laws for short-term, Airbnb holiday letting?
description: Before investing in Airbnb or short-term rentals on the Sunshine Coast, learn the council laws and restrictions that could impact your plans.
imageAlt: Person reading outdoors, symbolising short-term rental property lifestyle
tags: the rules for short stay holiday letting
local council laws for short stay holiday lettings
baxter and mason property buyers agent
baxter and mason property buyers agent sunshine coast
body:
Before buying an investment that you intend to use for short-term letting, holiday letting and Airbnb letting on the Sunshine coast, you need to know what the council laws and restrictions are.

Traditionally a residential property was built and zoned for people to live in for long periods of time. A regular home when designed and constructed with different building features included (eg fire warning system) compared to a building that is used for holiday or short-term rentals such as AirBnB, Stayz etc.

Using a house for short term accommodation changes the function of the house and has possible impacts on the surrounding area. Planning regulations require certain properties on Queensland’s popular Sunshine Coast to seek council approval before owners transform their dwellings into short-term rental accommodations.

Council laws and restrictions regarding short-term letting, holiday letting, and Airbnb letting on the Sunshine Coast may vary depending on the specific local government area (LGA) within the region.

Council in some LGAs applied 50% higher rates for short-term lettings as opposed to those charged to their long-term counterparts.

Therefore, it is important to consult with the relevant council in your area for accurate and up-to-date information.

Below are some general guidelines that may apply to short-term letting in the Sunshine Coast region:

Noosa Shire Council
As of April 2021, Noosa Shire Council implemented restrictions on short-term letting, requiring hosts to obtain a permit for properties in specific zones. Hosts are limited to a maximum of 180 nights per year for short-term letting in residential areas.
However, a permit is not required for-

- Units within an on-site managed complex (and managed by the on-site letting pool);
- Holiday houses where the premises is only used by the owner, family or friends for periodic holidays and is not used for commercial gain;
- Where the short-term letting is home hosted (owner resides permanently on site, and lets a bedroom, studio or hosts a student or similar). Traditional bed and breakfast accommodation or rural cabins also fall within this category.

Sunshine Coast Council
Under the Sunshine Coast Councils Planning Scheme, 2014, properties built prior to 2014 would be able to be rented out as a short-term or holiday rental, such as an Airbnb, as long as the dwelling is compliant with regulations and lawful.

Any properties built after 2014, specifically those located in low-density zones currently utilised as short-term accommodation, could be required to gain approval and may need to submit a Material Change of Use (MCU) or Development Approval (DA) application to council to receive approval to utilise the property as a holiday rental or short-term stay.

Other LGAs in the Sunshine Coast region
Each LGA within the Sunshine Coast may have its own specific laws and restrictions on short-term letting. It is recommended to contact the respective council or visit their official website to gather accurate information regarding regulations and requirements in that particular area.

Lastly, it is important to note that state-wide regulations may also impact short-term letting. For example, in Queensland, the State Government introduced new laws in 2019 that require hosts to register their property on the state's Short-Term Accommodation Register if they are offering short-term letting for stays of less than 30 consecutive days.

title: The Family Home Guarantee: Empowering Single Parents to Achieve Homeownership
description: Explore how the Family Home Guarantee helps single parents buy property and what it means for achieving homeownership sooner.
imageAlt: Modern house with pool, reflecting single parents achieving homeownership
tags: baxter and mason property buyers agent sunshine coast
body:
The Australian Government has recently launched an innovative initiative called the Family Home Guarantee, aimed at assisting single parents in their journey towards homeownership. This groundbreaking program allows eligible single parents to purchase a home with just a 2% house deposit, making the dream of owning a home more accessible and achievable.

Understanding the Family Home Guarantee:
The Family Home Guarantee is an Australian Government initiative designed to support single parents who aspire to own their own home. Traditionally, saving for a substantial house deposit has been a significant barrier for many individuals, particularly single parents who face unique financial challenges. However, this initiative aims to alleviate this burden by reducing the required deposit to a mere 2% of the property's value.

Eligibility Criteria:
To qualify for the Family Home Guarantee, single parents must meet certain criteria. These criteria include being an Australian citizen or permanent resident, having a dependent child, and meeting specific income thresholds (the applicant didn’t earn more than $125,000 in the previous financial year, excluding child support payments). By targeting single parents, the initiative recognizes the importance of stable housing for families and aims to provide a pathway to homeownership that was previously out of reach for many.

Benefits of the Family Home Guarantee:
The Family Home Guarantee offers numerous advantages to single parents looking to purchase their own home. Firstly, the reduced deposit requirement of just 2% allows single parents to enter the property market sooner, bypassing the need to save for a larger deposit. This not only accelerates the process of homeownership but also provides stability and security for families.

Additionally, the initiative provides an opportunity for single parents to build equity in their own property rather than paying rent, which can be a more financially sustainable option in the long run. By investing in their own home, single parents can create a stable environment for their children and potentially secure their financial future.

Application Process and Support:
The Government has streamlined the application process for the Family Home Guarantee to ensure a smooth and efficient experience for single parents. Interested individuals can apply through authorized lenders who participate in the program. These lenders will assess the eligibility of applicants and guide them through the necessary steps to secure a home loan under the Family Home Guarantee.

Furthermore, the government has also recognized the importance of providing ongoing support to single parents throughout their homeownership journey. Various resources, including financial counselling and educational programs, are available to help single parents make informed decisions and manage their finances effectively.

Conclusion:

The Family Home Guarantee is a game-changer for single parents, offering a realistic pathway to homeownership with a reduced deposit requirement of just 2%. By removing the financial barriers that have traditionally hindered single parents from entering the property market, this initiative empowers them to create a stable and secure environment for their families. The Australian Government's commitment to supporting single parents through this program is a testament to their dedication to fostering inclusive and sustainable communities.

title: First Home Owners Grant QLD - EXPLAINED
description: Understand how the First Home Owners Grant works in Queensland and how it can help you get into your first property sooner.

tags: first home owners grants queensland explained
baxter and mason property buyers agent
baxter and mason property buyers agent sunshine coast
body:
Let me break down the differences between the four awesome first home owner grants available in Queensland:

1. First Home Loan Deposit Scheme (FHLDS): This scheme helps you secure your dream home by allowing you to purchase it with a smaller deposit, as low as 5% without having to a pay for Lenders Mortgage Insurance (LMI). It's a fantastic opportunity for first-time buyers who may not have a large amount saved up.

2. First Home Super Saver Scheme (FHSSS): With this scheme, you can save money for your first home by making voluntary contributions to your superannuation fund, which can also provide tax benefits. The best part? These contributions are taxed at a lower rate, meaning you can save more towards your dream home. Your contributions can be up to $15,000 per year, with a maximum of $50,000 in total that you can access and be use towards the purchase of your first home.

3. Queensland First Home Owner's Grant: This grant is specifically designed to give a helping hand to first-time buyers in Queensland. It provides $30,000 (up until June 2024) towards the purchase or construction of your brand new first home (the property must have never been lived in to be eligible). It's a fantastic way to kickstart your homeownership journey!

4. Queensland Stamp Duty Concession: Stamp duty can be a hefty expense when buying a property, but with this concession, you can save some serious cash. It offers a reduced rate or in some cases an exemption on stamp duty, making it more affordable for first-time buyers to get into the property market.

An important note, before applying for and of the mentioned grants, you need to check your eligibility.

So, whether you're looking for a smaller deposit, a tax-efficient savings option, a generous grant, or a stamp duty concession, Queensland has got you covered with these four amazing first home owner grants. Happy house hunting!​

Why Queenslanders - not southerners - are driving the next wave of growth


For years, the narrative has been that the Sunshine Coast?s population boom is fuelled by an influx of people escaping Sydney and Melbourne. But the latest ABS internal?migration and regional?population data tells a very different story - and it?s one every buyer, investor, and property professional should understand.

According to the ABS, internal migration remains one of the strongest contributors to population change across Australia, with clear patterns emerging between capital cities and regional areas.

And here?s the headline: The Sunshine Coast?s biggest source of new residents is Greater Brisbane - followed closely by the rest of Queensland - not Victoria or New South Wales.

This shift has major implications for demand, pricing, infrastructure, and the types of properties people are seeking.


?? Where Are New Sunshine Coast Residents Coming From? (2025?2026)

While the ABS does not publish suburb?level inflow tables in the headline release, the broader internal?migration patterns are clear:

1. Greater Brisbane ? Sunshine Coast

Brisbane is one of only two capitals with net internal?migration gains in the latest ABS release. A significant portion of this movement flows north into the Sunshine Coast, driven by:

  • Lifestyle upgrades

  • Hybrid work

  • Schooling and family relocation

  • Housing affordability relative to Brisbane?s inner ring

2. Rest of Queensland ? Sunshine Coast

Regional Queensland continues to show strong mobility, with many residents moving toward coastal lifestyle hubs. This group now represents one of the largest migration cohorts into the Sunshine Coast.

3. Greater Melbourne & Greater Sydney (still strong, but no longer dominant)

ABS data shows both Sydney and Melbourne recorded net internal?migration losses, meaning more people left than arrived. While many still head to Queensland, the Sunshine Coast is no longer receiving the majority of its growth from southern capitals.

? Why This Matters for 2025?2026

1. Demand is becoming more localised

With Queenslanders driving the majority of migration, buyers are arriving with:

  • Local knowledge

3. Investors must rethink their assumptions

The ?Sydney/Melbourne exodus? narrative is outdated. The real growth engine is intra?Queensland movement, which tends to be:

  • More stable

  • Less interest?rate sensitive

  • More lifestyle?driven

4. Infrastructure planning will shift

More families relocating from Brisbane means increased demand for:

  • Schools

  • Transport links

  • Health services

  • Family?sized housing

?? What This Means for Buyers & Sellers

For Buyers

Competition will remain strong in suburbs close to schools, beaches, and lifestyle precincts. Local buyers are savvy ? meaning off?market access and negotiation strategy matter more than ever.

For Sellers

Your strongest buyer pool is now within Queensland, not interstate. Marketing strategies should reflect this shift.

For Investors

Look for areas aligned with family migration patterns - not just holiday demand.

?Final Word

Internal migration is reshaping the Sunshine Coast - and the biggest movers aren?t who most people think. Greater Brisbane and regional Queensland are driving the next chapter of growth, reshaping demand and creating new opportunities for strategic buyers.

title: Requirements when buying a property on a 491 Visa
description: Planning to buy on a 491 Visa? Learn the key requirements and restrictions for purchasing property in Queensland.
imageAlt: Large red question mark, symbolising property requirements for 491 visa buyers
body:
Baxter & Mason Property Buyers Agent Sunshine Coast was recently asked if it is possible to buy a property if the client is on a ‘491 Visa’ (pathway to permanent resident) in Queensland. The short answer is that it is possible but the following requirements must be met:

1. Eligibility for a home loan - You must meet the eligibility criteria for obtaining a home loan from a lender in Australia.

2. Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) approval - If you are a non-resident, non-Australian citizen, you will need to obtain FIRB approval to buy property in Australia.

3. Proof of income - You must have a stable income source in Queensland to demonstrate your ability to repay the home loan.

4. A valid visa - You must have a valid 491 visa and demonstrate that you have a pathway to permanent residency.

5. Sufficient funds - You must have sufficient funds to cover the deposit and purchase costs associated with buying a home in Queensland.

6. Legal assistance - It is recommended to seek legal advice to help you understand the legal and financial requirements of buying property in Queensland.

Macro due diligence generally takes a broad view of the property and its potential risks, while micro due diligence requires a more detailed and specific investigation of certain elements of the property.

Macro due diligence often encompasses an overall review and appraisal of the property, the surrounding area, the zoning, residential versus commercial, and market and capital trends.

Micro due diligence, on the other hand, looks more closely at elements such as the structural integrity of the building, the area’s occupancy rate, the tenant mix, leasing rules, maintenance and repair of the property, compliance with building regulations, and the financial records and history of the property.

It's important to understand the difference and choose the right strategy for your needs.

Tax Benefits
There are some tax benefits to owning an investment property, but they can be complicated. You'll need to understand the rules and regulations, and make sure you're taking advantage of all the deductions and allowances available to you.

Overall, buying an investment property can be a challenging and complex process. But with the right approach and a bit of patience, it can also be a rewarding and profitable investment.

title: The impact of the population explosion on property in QLD
description: Queensland’s population is booming. See how rapid growth is driving property demand and shaping future investment opportunities.

body:
South East Queensland has experienced a significant population explosion in recent years and the booming Queensland population is predicted to surpass 7 million by 2046.

It’s not just the southerners who moved up to sunny Queensland that are the only contributors to the explosion though, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, around 170,900 people migrated from overseas in 2021/22. Of those, 23,430 made the move to Queensland.

As you can imagine this population explosion has had a significant impact on the property market in this location. At a glance for the South East Queensland region the data shows that by 2046 there will be nearly 2.2 million more people which also means there will be a need for almost 900,000 new homes, that is 40,000 new homes per year in South East Queensland alone!

As a Sunshine Coast local, I have strong interest in the data for this region and in the Sunshine Coast Local Government Area – in the period from 2021 to 2046 there will be growth of 57.37%.

Let's discuss the key factors driving this population growth and the repercussions it has on the property market.

Population Growth
South East Queensland has been attracting a large number of both interstate and international migrants. The region offers a desirable lifestyle with a warm climate, beautiful beaches, and a strong job market. The population growth has been further fuelled by the affordability of housing compared to other major Australian cities.

Increased Demand
The population explosion has resulted in an increased demand for housing in the region. This surge in demand has led to a rise in property prices and rental rates. As the population continues to grow, the demand for housing is expected to persist, driving prices even higher.

Housing Affordability Challenges
The population explosion has placed additional pressure on housing affordability in South East Queensland. With increasing demand and limited supply, property prices have risen, making it more difficult for first-time buyers and lower-income earners to enter the market. This has led to concerns about housing affordability and the need for policies to address the issue.

Rental Market
The population boom has also impacted the rental market. As individuals and families move to the region, there is increased competition for rental properties, leading to rising rents. This can make it challenging for renters, particularly those on lower incomes, to find affordable housing.

Development and Infrastructure
To accommodate the growing population, there has been a surge in development and infrastructure projects in South East Queensland. New residential developments, apartment complexes, and infrastructure improvements, such as upgraded transportation networks and amenities, have been implemented to meet the demand. This development activity has not only provided additional housing supply but has also boosted the local economy.

Overall, South East Queensland's population explosion has had a profound impact on the property market. While it has created economic opportunities and new development, it has also posed challenges in terms of housing affordability. As the population continues to grow, it is crucial for policymakers and stakeholders to consider strategies that balance housing supply and demand to ensure sustainable and affordable housing options for all.

Are you considering buying an apartment? Have you considered the advantages and disadvantages of this decision?

Owning and living in an apartment has your normal costs associated with home ownership such as utilities, content insurance and council rates, but you also need to investigate any special levies for unexpected repairs or renovations.

One of the key factors to take into account is the body corporate fees. The body corporate fees, which are shared among all the apartment owners, cover expenses such as building insurance, common area maintenance, repair costs, and management fees.

While body corporate fees contribute to the overall upkeep and value of the property, these fees can vary greatly depending on the size and location, amenities provided, age and quality of the building/s and how many units are in the apartment complex.

This convenience of apartment living comes at a cost; therefore, it is essential to thoroughly review the body corporate fees and understand what they cover to ensure they align with your budget and expectations. Additionally, it’s equally important to inquire about the maintenance schedule, sinking fund and understand the potential costs involved to avoid any surprises down the line.

title: What is the difference?
description: Confused about property buying terms? We break down the key differences that every Sunshine Coast buyer should understand.

the difference between a selling agent and a buyers agent
body:
What is the difference between a real estate agent and a property buyer? Here at Baxter and Mason Property Buyers Agent, we have this question asked a lot!

A standard real estate sales agent in Queensland is licensed to work on behalf of the residential property seller to list and sell their property and represents the seller’s interests in the transaction. This real estate agent can help a buyer negotiate the purchase of the property but ultimately works for the seller’s best interest.

The general function of a real estate sales agent are:
• To estimate the selling price of a property
• To market property
• To show property
• To negotiate price and
• To affect a binding contract.

A buyer’s agent in Queensland is a licensed agent who is paid to protect the interests of buyers, and works solely for the buyer by researching, sourcing the property and negotiating the purchase price and terms and conditions of the purchase.

Buyer’s advocates strive to achieve the best price and terms for the buyer and do not represent either the seller or the landlord. They are a consulting agent that assists the buyer in making the best decision for their particular property needs.

The buyers advocate job is to:
• Qualify the purchasers’ ability to buy the property
• To search for properties within the price range and individual needs of the client
• To negotiate on behalf of the buyers and
• Assist with effecting of a binding contract

All legislation places a fiduciary duty to act in the best interest of their client. What this means is, if an agent is working for a seller/vendor, it is their job to achieve the highest price on the best terms for the seller. Whilst a buyer’s agent will attempt to obtain the lowest price on the best terms for their client. This prevents real estate sales agents from acting for both parties.

title: What needs to considered when applying for a home loan!
description: Applying for a home loan? Learn what lenders look for beyond income and how to boost your chances of approval.
imageAlt: Teacher with students, symbolising education on property home loans
tags: what needs to be considered when applying for a home loan
body:
When it comes to determining an individual's eligibility for a loan in Australia, financial lenders consider various factors beyond just income. While income is undoubtedly an essential criterion, lenders take a holistic approach to assess an applicant's overall financial position. Here are some additional factors considered during the loan assessment process:

1. Credit history: Lenders thoroughly analyse an applicant's credit score and credit history. Your ability to manage prior financial commitments, such as credit card payments, existing loans, and repayment history, plays a crucial role. A positive credit history demonstrates reliability, making lenders more likely to offer a loan.

2. Employment stability: Alongside income, lenders consider factors like the length and stability of your employment. A consistent employment history indicates a reliable income source and potential borrowing capacity.

3. Debt-to-income ratio: Lenders evaluate your debt-to-income ratio, which measures the amount of debt you have relative to your income. A lower debt-to-income ratio indicates a lesser burden of existing debt, increasing your chances of securing a loan.

4. Savings and assets: Your savings and assets, such as property, investments, and shares, can positively impact your loan eligibility. These act as collateral or demonstrate financial stability, assuring lenders of your repayment capabilities.

5. Expenses and living costs: Lenders account for your regular expenses and living costs to gauge your capacity to meet loan repayments comfortably. This includes factors like rent or mortgage repayments, utility bills, dependent expenses, and other financial commitments.

6. Age and employment type: Depending on the loan type, lenders may consider your age and employment type. Some loan products may have age restrictions, while employment stability in the case of self-employed individuals or contractors could be evaluated differently.

7. Loan purpose and security: The purpose of the loan and the security being offered may also influence eligibility. For instance, lending institutions often offer more favourable terms for property-secured loans than unsecured personal loans.

8. Legal and regulatory requirements: Lenders also consider legal and regulatory obligations. They ensure compliance with anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing regulations, verify your identity through KYC processes, and assess your eligibility with respect to responsible lending guidelines.

It is important to note that each lender may have its own specific criteria and weighting for these factors. Therefore, it is advisable to consider multiple options and seek professional advice to determine the best lender and loan product based on your individual circumstances.
